cards.b: Q = heart rate × stroke volume (ml or litres per minute).
Volume of blood pumped out of the left ventricle in one beat.

cards.f: Path of blood through the heart
cards.b: Vena cava, right atrium, right ventricle, pulmonary artery, lungs, pulmonary vein, left atrium, left ventricle, aorta.

cards.f: Which side of the heart is deoxygenated?
cards.b: The right side, which pumps to the lungs. The left side is oxygenated and pumps to the body.

cards.f: Why is the left ventricle wall thickest?
cards.b: It pumps blood around the whole body, so it needs more force.
Thick, muscular, elastic walls; narrow lumen; carries blood away from the heart under high pressure.
Thinner walls, wide lumen, valves to stop backflow; carries blood to the heart.
Walls one cell thick; allow exchange of gases, nutrients and waste with tissues.
Redirecting blood to working muscles (vasodilation) and away from non-essential organs (vasoconstriction) during exercise.
Diaphragm contracts and flattens; intercostals contract, ribs up and out; chest volume increases.
Diaphragm relaxes and domes; ribs down and in; chest volume decreases.
O₂ diffuses from alveoli into blood; CO₂ diffuses from blood into alveoli. Down concentration gradients.
Large surface area, walls one cell thick, many capillaries, moist.
Tidal volume = air in one breath. Minute ventilation = tidal volume × breathing rate.

short.q: Calculate the cardiac output of an athlete with a heart rate of 52 bpm and a stroke volume of 110 ml.
Explain the function of valves in the heart and in veins.
short.model: Valves make sure blood flows in one direction only and stop it flowing backwards.

short.q: Describe how the structure of capillaries helps gas exchange at the muscles.
short.model: Capillary walls are one cell thick, so the diffusion distance is very short. Oxygen diffuses into the muscle and carbon dioxide into the blood.
points: one cell thick / short diffusion distance

short.q: Describe what happens to heart rate, stroke volume and cardiac output when a person starts to run.
short.model: All three increase to deliver more oxygenated blood to the working muscles.
points: stroke volume and cardiac output increase

short.q: Explain how vascular shunting helps a footballer during a match.
short.model: Blood vessels to the leg muscles widen while those to the digestive system narrow, so more oxygen reaches the working muscles.
points: vasoconstriction to other organs / more oxygen to muscles
